s1.syndrome_frame: Chronic pruritic skin lesions with hyperkeratotic plaques
salient_findings: Pruritic lesions on the scrotum and buttock
Annular gray hyperkeratotic plaques with atrophic center and elevated edge
Hyperkeratosis, irregular papillomatosis, and parakeratotic columns on histopathology
key_facts: 10-year history of pruritic lesions
Lesions located on scrotum, buttock, groin, and intergluteal cleft
Previous treatment at local clinic with little improvement
No relevant medical history
No family history of similar skin problems
Normal or negative routine blood work, syphilis serologies, and HIV testing
Histopathological examination revealed hyperkeratosis and parakeratotic columns
Perivascular infiltration of lymphocytes in the dermis
No inguinal adenopathy

shortlist.label: Darier disease
shortlist.why_kept: Hyperkeratotic plaques and dyskeratotic keratinocytes are characteristic of Darier disease

shortlist.label: Grover disease
shortlist.why_kept: Pruritic lesions and hyperkeratotic plaques are consistent with Grover disease

shortlist.label: Hailey-Hailey disease
shortlist.why_kept: Hyperkeratotic plaques and perivascular infiltration of lymphocytes are seen in Hailey-Hailey disease

shortlist.label: Porokeratosis
shortlist.why_kept: Annular plaques with atrophic centers and hyperkeratotic edges are characteristic of porokeratosis

shortlist.label: Lichen simplex chronicus
shortlist.why_kept: Pruritic lesions and hyperkeratotic plaques are consistent with lichen simplex chronicus

raw.rationale: The presence of hyperkeratosis, irregular papillomatosis, parakeratotic columns (cornoid lamella), and dyskeratotic keratinocytes in the histopathological examination are characteristic features of porokeratosis, which is a disorder of keratinization.

rejected.label: Darier disease
rejected.why: While it involves dyskeratotic keratinocytes, Darier disease typically presents with greasy, crusted papules in seborrheic areas, not matching the described lesions.

rejected.label: Grover disease
rejected.why: It is characterized by sudden onset of pruritic papules, typically on the trunk, which doesn't fit the 10-year history and specific locations of the lesions in this case.

rejected.label: Hailey-Hailey disease
rejected.why: This condition is an inherited blistering skin condition, which doesn't match the description of hyperkeratotic plaques and the lack of family history.

rejected.label: Lichen simplex chronicus
rejected.why: While it can present with hyperkeratotic plaques, it is usually a result of chronic scratching and doesn't typically have the specific histopathological features seen in this case, like parakeratotic columns.
